messages.author: e14baef37a11434f
messages.subject: Iteration limit exceeded.  Algorithm failed.
parts:
I am running a bit of a complex/annoying analysis that has many studies pooled together. For most studies I want p, sig, and d to all be estimated independent of the other data, but for some, I am pooling p and sig.

The algorithm doesn’t seem to converge by the 200 limit. After iteration 200 I get "Iteration limit exceeded.  Algorithm failed.”

It looks within nlm() I can increase “iterlim”, but I don’t think I can pass this in oSCR.fit. I could also start the model again now, with the iteration 200 betas as the starting values.

Alternatively, does this failure to converge suggest an underlying issue with my parameterization ?

Best,
Clayton

messages.subject: RE: [oscr] Iteration limit exceeded.  Algorithm failed.
parts:
Hi Clayton,

 

I just pushed a quick fit. If you install the updated version from github, you will see there is a new argument (nlmiterlim =). The default is 200, but now you can up that. I need to generalize the function to be able to pass any nlm call via the ‘…’, but I keep seeing arguments for different optimizers preventing me from committing. I will commit soon and make this more flexible before the end of the year.

 

By the way, 200 I a lot. I wonder what happens when you add starting values? Id hope that is the fix you are looking for (i.e., more time to reach convergence). But, seeing your full model and the summary data (print.scrFrame(sf)) might give more food for thought/comment.

 

Chris

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Iteration limit exceeded.  Algorithm failed.
parts:
To be clear, it’s possible that with a weakly informed likelihood (i.e., too many parameters for the data) that increasing the iterations will not get you to a solution. More reasonable starting values could still leave you high and dry.

There are potentially further options to troubleshoot this problem depending on the optimizer used for the MLE. Mostly it’s just frustrating!

parts:
That’s right, the parameter estimates will be equivalent. With loop structures in R, there really isn’t an advantage to fitting the data all together if all parameters are replicate specific and you are not interested in model selection.

What I like to do is specify a state space with a really coarse resolution, coarser than is reasonable (too big for sigma). You can quickly learn some things from model fits, even if some parameter estimates will be poor.
